reading.body:
The Brandaleone Lab for Data and Visualization is attributed to Duke Libraries in Durham County, North Carolina, but its power capacity is not published. Research found no public specification of backend data center infrastructure, only references to user-facing computer stations in library buildings. Without published megawatt figures, this facility cannot be ranked against other AI infrastructure in North Carolina.

Duke Libraries operates enterprise and research computing supporting digital collections and archives for Duke University rather than commercial data center operations. The facility's power draw, IT load, and equipment type are not documented in public sources. No information is available on whether this site has grid capacity reserved for accelerator workloads or future AI scaling.

North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities, but only five have published power specifications totaling 50.3 MW. The Brandaleone Lab does not contribute to that published total. Without capacity data, this site cannot be assessed as a factor in the state's AI infrastructure or grid constraints.
